Serial-number comparison (RFC 1982): true when precedes .

member.name: M:Meziantou.Framework.DnsClient.Internal.DnssecValidator.GetClosestEncloser(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Meziantou.Framework.DnsClient.Response.Records.DnsNsecRecord},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Meziantou.Framework.DnsClient.Response.Records.DnsNsec3Record})
member.summary: Determines the closest encloser: the deepest ancestor of that provably exists.
member.remarks: For NSEC3 (RFC 5155 section 8.3) it is the deepest ancestor whose hash matches an NSEC3 owner. For NSEC it is derived from the covering record: the owner and next names both exist in the zone, so the longest suffix either shares with the queried name is an existing ancestor. Deriving it this way rather than demanding an exact owner match is what makes minimally-covering NSEC zones (RFC 4470) validate.

member.name: T:Meziantou.Framework.DnsClient.Protocol.DnsNameComparer
member.summary: Comparison of domain names in presentation format, done on the underlying wire octets.
member.remarks: Names are compared octet-wise after downcasing A-Z, per RFC 4034 section 6.1 and RFC 4343.
